newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks weak in morning after inching to high.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks weak in morning after inching to high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ventured into new record territory in early Thursday trade before giving back some of Wednesday's huge gains as the leading property and banking sectors slipped.
The Hang Seng Index was down 74.37 points, or 0.54 percent, at 13,692.28 after rising to an intra-day record high of 13,796.43, beating Wednesday's high of 13,771.54.
Turnover was HK$3.40 billion after the first hour of trade.
"It has gone up quite sharply," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
The Hang Seng posted its third-biggest point gain ever on Wednesday, rising 472.78 points.

"Investors are still digesting the bullish run we had yesterday," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. "Overall there is still a lot of interest to feed the market over 14,000, but this buying interest does not have to occur over two or three days."
Analysts said the strong property market and hopes of stable interest rates would continue to support share prices.

"There has been a lot of momentum built up over the last few weeks because there is a lot of portfolio rebalancing favouring the Hong Kong market due to the stable interest rate outlook," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"There are few alternatives in the region with Japan getting clobbered and Thailand still under pressure," he added.
Fernow said the Hong Kong government's move to preempt speculation in the property market was also positive since it should quell the possibility of the property market overheating.
The government said on Wednesday it welcomed voluntary moves by developers to curb rampant speculation and warned it would impose tougher measures if they proved insufficient.
"There is the possibility of a Chinese New Year rally allowing the market to continue to hit record levels," said Fernow.

Despite blue chip weakness, shares in Great Eagle Holdings rose HK$0.90 to HK$34.90 after the company posted net profit for the year to September 30, 1996, of HK$1.06 billion compared with HK$820.04 million.
Analysts said the stock was trading at a discount to its net asset value of around HK$44.60 per share. "It is not overpriced now," said Rossiter.
Shares in HSBC Holdings slipped HK$1.00 to HK$178.00, after climbing HK$8.50 on Wednesday.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong was down HK$2.25 at HK$75.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.75 to HK$94.25.
